setting: You all work in the accounts team of a small firm in Leeds, England, handling supplier payments and month-end close. You have worked together for about three years and know each other's routines well enough to share a group chat. Daniel keeps the master spreadsheet of supplier invoices that the month-end run depends on, and everyone knows it is due to go to Tom by the end of Friday. The last thing you talked about in the chat, a week or so ago, was whether the Leeds Rhinos had won at the weekend.

Priya.who: 34, woman, the team-mate who needs Daniel's file
Priya.knows: You know Daniel is the colleague who owns the invoice spreadsheet and is usually dependable, though slow to reply on Fridays. You know Sophie as a team-mate you get on with well and Tom as the senior team-mate who signs off the month-end pack.
Priya.texts: You mostly write in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, dropping them only when you are rushed. You use an emoji now and then and keep messages short.
ex: Did you get the bins sorted or is that still on you?
Ha, Sophie, you always say that and then you're the first one in.
Sorry, I'm in a meeting until half two, will catch up after
Tom, have you got five minutes this afternoon?

Daniel.who: 41, man, the team-mate who holds the invoice spreadsheet
Daniel.knows: You know Priya as a careful colleague who reconciles quickly, and Sophie as the one who keeps the team on time. You know Tom as the senior team-mate who has trusted you with the file for years.
Daniel.texts: You text in lowercase most of the time when you are busy, with few full stops and the occasional thumbs-up. You rarely use emoji and usually keep messages brief.
ex: ok, will do
sorry, been on the phone all morning
did anyone see the email about the car park?
can someone cover the 2pm for me, school pick up
thanks Tom, I'll sort it

Sophie.who: 29, woman, the team-mate who keeps the team organised
Sophie.knows: You know Priya as a friend from the team who sits near you and Daniel as the quiet, reliable one who holds the file. You know Tom as the senior team-mate who is fair and approachable.
Sophie.texts: You text casually with capitals and punctuation most of the time, and you use emoji quite often. Your messages are short and you sometimes send a couple in a row.
ex: omg it's freezing in here

Priya, I'll bring your stuff in tomorrow
Tom, do you want me to take the call at 10 or are you?

Tom.who: 52, man, the senior team-mate who signs off the month-end pack
Tom.knows: You know Priya as a sharp, dependable colleague who keeps her head down and gets things done, and Daniel as the one who holds the file and has done so for years. You know Sophie as the energetic one who keeps everyone talking.
Tom.texts: You mostly write in plain full sentences with proper punctuation and no emoji, and you keep messages short. Now and then you add a brief "thanks" or "cheers" but rarely anything more casual.
ex: Thanks, that's helpful

topic: You need Daniel's spreadsheet of supplier invoices before the end of Friday.
